solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Riddler cross after hips broken by Batman, finally (6)

indicators.note: hips are smashed up, with the next letter thrown in among them
the cross comes after the rest
takes the last letter of Batman

blocks.note: anagram fodder
last letter of Batman, joining the fodder
a cross is an X

annotation.surface: A cross Riddler, hips broken in a fight with Batman.
annotation.walkthrough: The Riddler is Batman's foe, but the definition is the Sphinx, the original riddler, whose riddle Oedipus answered.
annotation.definitionFit: The Sphinx of Greek myth killed travellers who could not answer its riddle.

entries.clue: Take action to welcome Europeans and Africans (8)

indicators.note: SUE takes the Europeans in

blocks.note: to sue is to take legal action
Danes are Europeans

annotation.surface: An instruction to act by welcoming visitors from Europe and Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: Take action is the legal sense: to bring an action against someone is to sue them.
annotation.definitionFit: The Sudanese are people from Sudan in Africa.

entries.clue: Back uniform for religious adherent (5)

blocks.note: hind = back, as in hind legs
Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone supports school uniform for religious reasons.
annotation.walkthrough: Back looks like a verb meaning support; it is the adjective, as in hind legs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a follower of any faith is an adherent, and Hinduism is the faith here.

entries.clue: Centre of upside-down cake (3)

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning BUN over makes it read bottom to top

blocks.note: a bun is a small cake

annotation.surface: The middle of a pineapple upside-down cake.
annotation.walkthrough: Upside-down cake is a real pudding, so the phrase reads as one thing; here the upside-down is an instruction to flip the bun.
annotation.definitionFit: The nub of something is its central point.

entries.clue: Glass boat (8)

blocks.note: a tall glass for sherry or beer
a sailing ship with two or more masts

annotation.walkthrough: A schooner is both a tall glass for sherry or beer and a sailing ship with two or more masts.
annotation.definitionFit: Schooner names both a drinking glass and a fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel.

entries.clue: Keen kiosk gets rid of last sparkler (7)

indicators.note: the kiosk drops its final letter

blocks.note: to keen is to wail in grief
STALL, a kiosk, without its last L

annotation.surface: An eager kiosk owner sells off the last sparkler.
annotation.walkthrough: Keen reads as an adjective meaning eager; it is the verb, to lament loudly.
annotation.definitionFit: Crystal sparkles, so it can be called a sparkler, as diamonds are.

entries.clue: Boss to get the drinks in? (5,6)

blocks.note: to boss people is to give them orders
to get the drinks in is to buy a set of drinks for the whole group at the bar

annotation.walkthrough: Split the second word: to order a round is to buy drinks for everyone in your group at the pub.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: bossing people is ordering them about, and ordering a round is buying drinks at the pub.

entries.clue: Fresh tear in cheap paper (9)

blocks.note: fresh = new
to tear along is to sprint

annotation.surface: A new rip in a flimsy sheet of paper.
annotation.walkthrough: Tear wants to be a rip in the paper; it is the other word, a dash at full speed.
annotation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the cheap, low-grade paper newspapers are printed on.

entries.clue: Guy ran off in piece of sci-fi literature (3,3)

indicators.note: the letters of GUY RAN go off, out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A man runs off into a science-fiction story.
annotation.walkthrough: Piece is slang for a gun, so a piece of sci-fi literature is a weapon found in such stories.
annotation.definitionFit: A ray gun is the energy weapon of science fiction.

entries.clue: Business with a commodity initially embraced by millennials? (6)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of commodity
GEN Y holds the C inside it

blocks.note: used as printed
first letter of commodity
Generation Y is another name for millennials

annotation.surface: A company trading in something millennials have taken to.
annotation.walkthrough: Generation Y, born roughly 1981 to 1996, is the usual label for millennials.
annotation.definitionFit: An agency is a business providing a service, such as a travel agency.

entries.clue: Beach vehicle, due to bear north, full of problems (4,5)

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so DUE carries N inside it like a load

blocks.note: used as printed
N = north
buggy software is full of bugs

annotation.surface: A beach car expected to head north, but breaking down all the time.
annotation.walkthrough: Bear here means carry, not the animal or turning a direction.
annotation.definitionFit: A dune buggy is a light open car built for driving on sand.

entries.clue: Carry out crooked payment for union (5)

blocks.note: to carry out a task is to do it
wry = twisted, crooked

annotation.surface: Someone makes a dishonest payment to a trade union.
annotation.walkthrough: Union reads as a trade union; it is marriage.
annotation.definitionFit: A dowry is the money or property a bride's family pays on her marriage.

entries.clue: Returns to an irregular galactic body (7,4)

indicators.note: the letters of RETURNS TO AN are put out of regular order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A strange object in space comes back again and again.
annotation.walkthrough: Returns looks like the verb; it is simply eleven letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A neutron star is the very dense collapsed core of a massive star.

entries.clue: Flower and wine stolen before game (3-3,5)

indicators.note: the first two pieces come before the game

blocks.note: red = red wine
hot = stolen, as in hot goods
poker is a card game

annotation.surface: Flowers and wine taken before a match.
annotation.walkthrough: Hot for stolen is everyday slang: hot goods are too recently stolen to sell openly.
annotation.definitionFit: The red-hot poker is a garden plant with tall spikes of orange-red flowers.

entries.clue: Musical more popular in Uruguay at first? (3)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of popular, in, Uruguay

annotation.surface: A show that went down better in Uruguay at its opening.
annotation.walkthrough: Musical looks like a show; here it modifies more, meaning the word used in music for more.
annotation.definitionFit: Più is the Italian musical direction for more, as in più forte, louder.

entries.clue: Support Times on position trader takes on market (5,2)

indicators.note: in an across entry, BY is placed on, after, STAND

blocks.note: a stall a trader sets up at a market is a stand
times = by, as in three by four

annotation.surface: Backing the Times newspaper's stance while a trader goes to market.
annotation.walkthrough: Times is not the newspaper; it is multiplication, read as by.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the loyal sense: standing by a friend in trouble is supporting them.

entries.clue: Gold character left uncovered (2,7)

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
someone's character is their nature
L = left

annotation.surface: A golden figure stands exposed.
annotation.walkthrough: Uncovered reads as a verb, revealed; here it is the adjective, naked.
annotation.definitionFit: Au naturel, French for in the natural state, means naked.

entries.clue: Poet fooling around endlessly (6)

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: LARKING without its last G

annotation.surface: A poet who never stops messing about.
annotation.walkthrough: Philip Larkin was an English poet, best known for The Whitsun Weddings.
annotation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was a twentieth-century English poet.

entries.clue: Mike stops to make a meal in the afternoon (5,3)

indicators.note: M plugs a gap inside CREATE

blocks.note: to make is to create
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet
used as printed

annotation.surface: Mike stops what he is doing to cook an afternoon meal.
annotation.walkthrough: Stops means plugs, not halts: M goes into the middle of CREATE. A cream tea is the British afternoon spread of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the British cream tea of scones, jam and clotted cream is taken mid-afternoon.

entries.clue: Inter Milan’s leader bet on getting beaten (6)

indicators.note: the letters are knocked about

blocks.note: first letter of Milan
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Backing Inter Milan to lose.
annotation.walkthrough: Inter Milan is the football club, but Inter alone is the verb, to bury.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: inter and entomb both mean to place a body in a grave or tomb.

entries.clue: Italian city’s expression of gratitude for drinks supplier (7)

blocks.note: Bari is a port in southern Italy, plus the S of the possessive
ta is British informal for thank you

annotation.surface: An Italian town thanks the firm that supplies its drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe S counts as a letter here.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the barista behind a coffee bar supplies espresso drinks.

entries.clue: Block board game piece (7)

blocks.note: to block a move is to answer it with one of your own
a disc moved round a board, as in ludo

annotation.walkthrough: To counter a move is to block it; a counter is also a disc moved round a board.
annotation.definitionFit: Counter is both the verb for blocking an attack and a playing piece.

entries.clue: Church exam for singers (6)

blocks.note: CH = church
an oral is a spoken exam

annotation.surface: A church test for choir members.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase, not a noun: choral music is music for singers.
annotation.definitionFit: Choral means written for or sung by a choir.

entries.clue: Secret police’s period of inactivity (6)

blocks.note: the Stasi were East Germany's secret police
the S of the possessive

annotation.surface: A time when the secret police do nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive S joins the name to make the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stasis, from the Greek for standing, names a state where nothing moves or changes.

entries.clue: Bit of needlework in gallery shunned by European (3)

annotation.definitionNote: TAT is a verb, to make tatting; the definition reads as a noun

indicators.note: the E is avoided, left out

blocks.note: TATE, the London gallery, without E for European

annotation.surface: A piece of embroidery in an art gallery that a European ignores.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tate is the London art gallery group. Tatting is lace made by knotting thread with a shuttle.
annotation.definitionFit: To tat is to make tatting, a form of knotted lace needlework.

entries.clue: Show fairy strange god (6,5)

blocks.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth
odd = strange
Rama is a Hindu god

annotation.surface: A fairy displays a peculiar deity.
annotation.walkthrough: Show reads as a verb, display; it is the noun, a television show.
annotation.definitionFit: A period drama is a show set in a past era.

entries.clue: A foreign greeting set up another? (5)

annotation.definitionNote: defined by reference to the foreign greeting in the wordplay: ALOHA is another one

indicators.note: in a down entry, A HOLA is lifted to read bottom to top

blocks.note: used as printed
hola is Spanish for hello

annotation.surface: Someone abroad says hello and wonders about saying it again.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversal takes in the A as well as HOLA. The question mark flags that the definition leans on the wordplay: hola is one foreign greeting, aloha is another.
annotation.definitionFit: Aloha is the Hawaiian greeting, another foreign hello.

entries.clue: Island not featured in Scream film (5)

indicators.note: the I is absent from the word

blocks.note: SHRIEK, a scream, without I for island

annotation.surface: An island is missing from the Scream horror film.
annotation.walkthrough: Scream film reads as the horror title; the film is Shrek and Scream is just a shriek.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Shrek is the 2001 animated film about an ogre.

entries.clue: Room left for launch zone (9)

blocks.note: room = space
port is the left side of a ship

annotation.surface: Space set aside for a product launch.
annotation.walkthrough: Left is not departed; it is the nautical side.
annotation.definitionFit: A spaceport is a site from which spacecraft are launched.

entries.clue: Introspective music contributing to pensive mood (3)

indicators.note: the answer is made up from parts of the words that follow

blocks.note: pensivE MOod

annotation.surface: Moody music feeding a thoughtful state of mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is apt in its own right: emo is known for confessional, brooding songs.
annotation.definitionFit: Emo is a style of rock music with emotional, introspective lyrics.

entries.clue: Ancient way of cooking lard is OK (4,4)

indicators.note: the letters are worked over, as ingredients are

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An old recipe says it is fine to cook with lard.
annotation.walkthrough: Way reads as method; it is a route.
annotation.definitionFit: The Silk Road was the ancient trade route linking China with the Mediterranean.

entries.clue: Person at academy exhibits work (6)

indicators.note: the phrase shows the answer inside it

blocks.note: perSON AT Academy

annotation.surface: A student at an art academy puts on a show of their work.
annotation.walkthrough: Academy and exhibits paint an art school show; the work is a piece of music.
annotation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical work, typically for one or two instruments.
